text: Continuous integration (CI) is a practice in software development where developers regularly merge their code changes into a shared repository. Each time code is added, automated builds start immediately, and the system compiles the new code without human help. During these builds, automated tests run to check that everything works correctly. This approach helps teams catch issues early, before they become serious problems. CI pipelines organise these steps into a clear sequence, such as building, testing, and reporting results. As a result, developers receive fast feedback and can fix bugs quickly, which keeps the software stable and the whole team more productive.
